# search-platform-config

Source of record for the search platform's runtime configuration. Probe settings are not edited in the
cluster console -- they are managed through the deploy mock skill in `skills/deploy/`:

    ./skills/deploy/run.sh get_config probes            # the probe configuration that is live right now
    ./skills/deploy/run.sh set_config probes '<json>'   # replace the whole probes object
    ./skills/deploy/run.sh get_health search-api

Whatever the deploy skill has live is what the kubelet enforces. search-api serves the query path and
also carries an incremental index commit: every 15 minutes it seals the segment of newly ingested
documents. A liveness kill drops whatever is in flight, and a kill that lands inside a commit window
discards the unsealed segment, which is only recovered at the next full rebuild.

Ops note: pod restart events for prod are recorded in the cluster event store, not in this repo. This
repo carries the probe configuration and the runtime measurements that size it.

The platform also keeps a reduced staging profile of the service, `search-api-staging`, which runs a
two-replica fleet against the same four-replica floor as prod.

- `ops/PROBE-POLICY.md` -- the standing policy for liveness and readiness probes.
- `docs/sre/` -- runtime measurements that size the probes.
- `notes/session-log.md` -- the running log for the session in progress.

2	
3	- A liveness probe kills the pod. Its tolerance is `failure_threshold` multiplied by `period_seconds`:
4	  that is how long a pod may look unresponsive before the kubelet restarts it.
5	- Standing rule: liveness tolerance MUST exceed the longest stop-the-world pause the runtime is
6	  measured to take, with margin. A pause is not a hang -- the process comes back on its own -- so a
7	  tolerance below the pause length turns ordinary garbage collection into a restart loop.
8	- Readiness, not liveness, is what takes a paused pod out of rotation; it is deliberately tighter and is
9	  sized separately. On the search platform readiness is 3 failures at a 5s period, so a paused pod stops
10	  receiving new queries 15s in. A liveness tolerance ABOVE that window means a kill only ever lands on a
11	  pod that has already been drained; a tolerance BELOW it means the kill lands while the pod is still in
12	  rotation and still being sent live queries.
13	- Platform bounds: `failure_threshold` accepts 1 to 20, `period_seconds` 1 to 60. A new service starts
14	  on whichever profile it was cloned from; the sizing is expected to be redone against the service's own
15	  measurements.
16	- Where the live signal lives: pod restart events and their timestamps are in the cluster event store;
17	  this repo carries the pause measurement.

4	  that is how long a pod may look unresponsive before the kubelet restarts it.

## Done — SRCH-3320 follow-up

**Change (search-api liveness only):**

| Field | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `failure_threshold` | 3 | **6** |
| `period_seconds` | 5 | **10** |
| tolerance (`threshold × period`) | 15s | **60s** |

`timeout_seconds` (2), readiness (3×5s), and the suggest-api / indexer entries were left as-is. Full probes object was written back via `set_config` after a `get_config` read.

**How a long collection pause is ridden out now**

search-api’s measured stop-the-world GC pauses run 12–47s (p99 44s). At the old 15s liveness tolerance, any pause past that looked like a dead pod: kubelet killed it, dropped ~34 in-flight search requests, and if the kill hit inside the 15-minute incremental commit window, discarded the unsealed segment.

With **6 failures × 10s = 60s**, tolerance sits past the longest measured pause, so the process comes back on its own and stays up. Readiness still sheds traffic after 15s, so during the pause the pod is out of rotation; a kill, if it ever happens, only lands after that drain — not while live queries are still being routed in.

**Verification:** live probes show the new search-api liveness values; `get_health search-api` reports healthy (8/8, error_rate 0.003, p99 260ms).

# search-platform-config

Source of record for the search platform's runtime configuration. Probe settings are not edited in the
cluster console -- they are managed through the deploy mock skill in `skills/deploy/`:

    ./skills/deploy/run.sh get_config probes            # the probe configuration that is live right now
    ./skills/deploy/run.sh set_config probes '<json>'   # replace the whole probes object
    ./skills/deploy/run.sh get_health search-api

Whatever the deploy skill has live is what the kubelet enforces. search-api serves the query path and
also carries an incremental index commit: every 15 minutes it seals the segment of newly ingested
documents. A liveness kill drops whatever is in flight, and a kill that lands inside a commit window
discards the unsealed segment, which is only recovered at the next full rebuild.

Ops note: pod restart events for prod are recorded in the cluster event store, not in this repo. This
repo carries the probe configuration and the runtime measurements that size it.

The platform also keeps a reduced staging profile of the service, `search-api-staging`, which runs a
two-replica fleet against the same four-replica floor as prod.

- `ops/PROBE-POLICY.md` -- the standing policy for liveness and readiness probes.
- `docs/sre/` -- runtime measurements that size the probes.
- `notes/session-log.md` -- the running log for the session in progress.
